 Toyota’s Station Wagon in Disguise Finally Fulfills Its Longroof Promise
 The automaker’s new build brings the stance and style the Crown Signia needs in order to really turn heads.
 Toyota 
 By Gray Van Dyke 
 Published 20 hours ago 
 ·
 Share 
 See more of our coverage in your search results 
 If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more 
 With its sleek bodywork and extended proportions, the Toyota Crown Signia has always given station wagon , even if its ride height parks it squarely in crossover territory.
 However, that doesn’t mean the vehicle is a lost cause. A few choice tweaks and it has the potential to realize its longroof promise once and for all.
 The Crown Signia GT-S Concept is a very different beast to the production vehicle. Toyota 
 Just take the concept that Toyota is bringing to SEMA 2026, as an example.
 A sporty Signia redux
 Toyota is calling it the Crown Signia GT-S Concept. If that moniker sounds familiar, it’s because the automaker brought a Camry of the same persuasion to last year’s show .
 The red accents really pop against the custom-mixed dark gray metallic paint. Toyota 
 True to the designation, this means the Crown Signia adopts a much sportier vibe. Around the outside, Toyota Motorsports Garage added widebody fenders, reshaped headlight surrounds and a revised rear end.
 It’s a highly transformative look, and details like the louvers on the front wings, the aggressive diffuser and the side skirts push the combination even further. Toyota even reworked the exhaust with trapezoidal tips integrated into the rear aero package.
 Toyota’s Crown Signia reads total station wagon when it sits five inches lower. Toyota 
 Yet, at the same time, the Crown Signia still presents a refined result. Toyota custom-mixed a dark gray metallic paint with some added flake, and tasteful red accents complement the hue inside and out.
 Low-slung SUV style
 Although Toyota didn’t mention any powertrain upgrades as part of the Crown Signia GT-S Concept’s overhaul, it does bring more than a fancy body kit and a new coat of paint.
 Toyota reworked the interior to give the Crown Signia some performance-inspired upholstery touches. Toyota 
 To achieve the low-slung stance, it rides on a set of custom one-off Motion Control Suspension coilovers. Toyota says this allows it to roll almost five full inches lower than stock.
 What’s more, it benefits from improved stopping power thanks to a set of front and rear brake calipers pulled off a Lexus RX 500h F Sport. The build team had to specially adapt the setup to make it fit. 
 The rear diffuser is one of the more dramatic aero modifications. Toyota 
 Rolling on some 21-inch HRE wheels, it’s only made better by the 295mm Toyo tires. According to Toyota, this means it brings an extra 20 percent of contact compared to the factory set.
 Even if it does roll with the same 2.5-liter four-cylinder hybrid powertrain as the production version, these changes should help make the most of that combined 240 horsepower output.
 The custom HRE wheels hide brake calipers pulled from a Lexus RX 500h F Sport. Toyota 
 Toyota hasn’t announced any plans to bring the Crown Signia GT-S Concept to market, though you’ll be able to catch it showcased at SEMA.
